evals.prompt: Style a branded <select> element that matches our design system without a heavy JS library.
evals.expected_behavior: Checks the static references/css.md file for the current selectors/scoping pattern before improvising, and recommends the modern base-select appearance approach instead of a legacy JS-replacement select.
assertions: Consults references/css.md (or an equivalent modern-web-guidance lookup) before proposing an implementation
Recommends appearance: base-select with ::picker(select) rather than a custom div-based dropdown
Adapts the pattern to the project's framework instead of pasting guide code verbatim

evals.prompt: Animate a dialog sliding in and fading out when it opens and closes, using the native <dialog> element.
evals.expected_behavior: Uses the two-step dynamic retrieval flow (search then retrieve) via the modern-web-guidance CLI to find the specific animate-to/from-top-layer guide rather than inventing an animation approach from training memory.
assertions: Runs `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest search` with an action-oriented query before answering
Retrieves the matched guide id with `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve` before implementing
Implements the top-layer/::backdrop animation pattern rather than a generic opacity-only transition

evals.prompt: Add a visually-hidden utility class for screen-reader-only text on this page.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes the topic is already covered by the static references/accessibility.md file and uses that directly instead of running the dynamic search/retrieve CLI flow for a topic the static references already answer.
assertions: Does not invoke the dynamic search/retrieve CLI when the static accessibility reference already covers the pattern
Recommends the clip-path: inset(50%) visually-hidden pattern rather than position: absolute; clip: rect(0,0,0,0)

evals.prompt: Add a form with autofill support and error messages that only appear after the user has interacted with a field.
evals.expected_behavior: Delivers a form implementation using post-interaction validation styling instead of the eager :invalid/:valid pseudo-classes, matching Baseline Widely Available guidance and noting any fallback for Newly/Limited Availability features used.
assertions: Uses :user-invalid/:user-valid rather than :invalid/:valid for validation UX
Confirms the chosen features are Baseline Widely Available or explicitly calls out fallback needed for Newly/Limited Availability features
Notes verification via the project's lint/test/browser checks once code lands

evals.prompt: Review this existing checkout UI for visual polish — tighten spacing, alignment, and shadow consistency.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes the concrete visual-polish review away from modern-web-guidance's API/pattern guidance and toward make-interfaces-feel-better, since this skill covers implementing platform patterns rather than polishing an existing UI's visual detail.
assertions: Does not run the modern-web-guidance search/retrieve workflow for a pure visual-polish review
Recommends make-interfaces-feel-better for the concrete visual-polish task instead

evals.prompt: This dialog component throws a runtime TypeError as soon as it opens — figure out why and fix it.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes the runtime-error debugging task to systematic-debugging rather than treating it as a modern-web-guidance API selection question.
assertions: Does not treat the runtime error investigation as a web-platform-pattern lookup task
Recommends systematic-debugging (or an equivalent debugging workflow) for the runtime error instead
